Subject: Request: quota increase for Orlando launch

Hi Marissa,

We’re ramping up for our Orlando product launch on 2026-03-15 and expect a spike in inference traffic for the first 72 hours. Our initial estimate is ~1.2M tokens/hour peak across 8k concurrent sessions, tapering to ~300k tokens/hour after day three. Can Redwood provide a temporary quota/rate-limit increase for our Hosted account and confirm any per-minute burst constraints?

Attached is our traffic profile and an initial capacity plan. We’re on a tight timeline and need confirmation by EOD 2026-03-03 so we can finalize the go/no-go.

Thanks,
Amanda Lopez
Head of Integrations, GlowAI

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: quota increase for Orlando launch -- triage + asks

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick assessment after a run against the upcoming capacity window: we can support a temporary bump but with the following constraints and operational steps:

- Proposed temporary limits for GlowAI (72h window):
  * Token throughput: increase from 150k -> 1.5M tokens/hour (soft enforcement at 1.2M, hard cut at 1.7M)
  * Concurrent sessions: allow up to 9k sessions (current plan supports 6k)
- Implementation: create a per-customer policy in the routing layer with burst token-bucket (burst capacity 2x base for first 15 minutes of each hour)
- Monitoring: enable per-route latency/cost alerts and an automatic rollback if error rate > 2.5% or p50 latency > 650ms for 10m window
- Risk: small bump to shared Dedicated pool usage on 2026-03-15. If other large customers spike the same day, we may see degraded p95s for non-Dedicated accounts.

Attachments: capacity_plan_orlando_v1.xlsx (I added an engineering tab with suggested node incrementing and rollback triggers).

Next steps: Jordan — confirm customer can accept the monitoring/rollback conditions. Laura — can you confirm whether enabling automated fallback to quantized model B is acceptable for the first 24h?

-Vivek
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Quick product notes:

- Fallback: auto-route to quantized model B is acceptable for first 24 hours provided we label prediction confidence in responses. Product wants a teardown of any quality drift metrics post-launch (we’ll run evals against the agreed prompt set).
- Billing/SLA: this is an exception — any credits for sustained degradation will be calculated against the standard Hosted SLA. We’ll need CS to record acceptance in the MAP; no automatic crediting.
- Telemetry: please ensure we capture token-level and route-level logs for the 72h window and persist them to the customer’s retention bucket for 30 days.

Note: if GlowAI expects sustained traffic beyond the 72h window we should convert them to a Dedicated commitment.

-Laura
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: quota increase for Orlando launch — confirmation and next steps

Amanda — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming Redwood will enable a temporary quota increase under the following operational terms: 

- Window: 2026-03-15 00:00 UTC through 2026-03-18 00:00 UTC (72 hours)
- Limits: soft cap at 1.2M tokens/hour, hard cap at 1.7M tokens/hour; concurrent sessions up to 9k
- Enforcement and rollback: burst token-bucket policy + automated rollback if error rate > 2.5% or p50 latency > 650ms for 10m
- Fallback: during sustained pressure, traffic will auto-route to quantized model B for the first 24 hours (quality labels included).
- Monitoring & comms: we’ll add you to the incident Slack channel and have on-call SREs monitor token-level dashboards; Jordan will lead the MAP and CS comms.

I’ve filed the quota_change_request_form.pdf and the ops request (QR-9876). Please sign the enclosed MAP (DocuSign link to follow) and confirm the final peak window.

If GlowAI needs a larger or longer commitment we should discuss Dedicated capacity — Jordan can follow up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
